name: hero-form-section
purpose: The opening band of a lead-capture page, where the form is the reason for the page: the hero copy and a list of highlights on one side, the form on the other, above the fold, with the client strip on the floor. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'hero-form-section', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `hero`, `hero-title`, `feature-item`, `field`, `input`, `select`, `phone-input`, `textarea`, `button` and `alert`. The fields are data: each entry of `fields` picks its control by `type`, so the Contact page and the Under attack page are the same block with different `fields`. The block never sends: it validates the fields locally (required fields and the email format, with the messages from `messages`) and on a valid submit emits `submit` with the event and the values keyed by field `name`; the site posts them and reports the outcome back through `loading`, `submitted` and `failed`.
useWhen: Use HeroFormSection when the page exists to capture a lead and the form sits above the fold.
To open a page whose purpose is a lead form, such as Contact sales or Under attack.
avoidWhen: For a newsletter sign-up with one email field → use `newsletter-section`.
For an opening band with calls to action and no form → use `hero-section`, which takes every other marketing page opening.
related: `newsletter-section` — the other form section; same `submit` and state contract.
`alert` — renders the success and failure messages.
bestPractices: Give every field a unique `name`; it is the key of the submitted value.
Mark half-width fields in pairs so each row stays full.

Set `visuallyHiddenLabel` on a field the page labels by its placeholder alone (azion.com's phone field): the label stays the control's accessible name for assistive tech but is not drawn, so give that field a `placeholder` that says what to type.

Keep the headline to a short phrase; the band sets it on a narrower measure than the description (`--container-md`), so "Grow as an Azion Partner" breaks over two lines as on the site. There is no width prop to tune.
Set `loading` while the values are sent, then `submitted` or `failed` with the outcome.

props.name: messages
props.doc: Copy of the form outcomes: `{ missing, invalidEmail, success, error }`.

props.name: titleHighlight
props.doc: Opening words of the headline, painted in the brand accent.

props.name: title
props.doc: Page headline, rendered as the page `h1`; the band renders nothing when empty.

props.name: descriptionLink
props.doc: A link continuing the description inline, such as a phone line; `{ label, href }`. Omitted when absent.

props.name: descriptionAfter
props.doc: Copy after the inline link, closing the description's sentence.

props.name: primaryAction
props.doc: First button under the copy; `{ label, href, trailing?, target? }`. Shown only with a label and a link.

props.name: secondaryAction
props.doc: Second, outlined button beside the first; `{ label, href, trailing?, target? }`. Shown only with a label and a link.

props.name: anchor
props.doc: In-page id set on the band so a `#hash` link can scroll to it.

props.name: items
props.doc: The highlights under the description, in order; each is `{ icon, title, description }`. The list renders only when there are items.

props.name: formAriaLabel
props.doc: Accessible name of the field group, read as its legend.

props.name: fields
props.doc: The form fields in order; each is `{ name, type, label, placeholder?, required?, half?, options?, country?, visuallyHiddenLabel? }`; `visuallyHiddenLabel` keeps the label as the accessible name but does not draw it.

props.name: marqueeMarks
props.doc: Registry names of the client marks, in order; the marquee renders only when there are marks.

props.name: loading
props.doc: The site is sending the values: the button shows its loading state and a submit is ignored.

props.name: submitted
props.doc: The site sent the values: the form gives way to `messages.success`.

props.name: failed
props.doc: The site could not send the values: `messages.error` shows under the form.

events.name: submit
events.notes: Fired on a valid submit, not while `loading`; `values` holds every field by `name`, trimmed, with a phone number prefixed by its dial code. The block never sends it.
